g.title: public.form_links
g.text: A tokenized link to one form version. NO subject means a prospect link (the prospect_intake row is created when they submit, not now — issuing creates nothing, so an unanswered link leaves no phantom prospect in the review queue). client_id set means an existing client's waiver. Single-use: consumed_at is claimed atomically by submit_form_response, never by the route.

FROZEN AT ISSUE. The link points at the exact version the recipient will answer, so publishing a new version between sending and submitting cannot change their questions or the sensitive flags their answers are split against.

The only authorization the public submission path has. Unguessable (gen_random_uuid), single-use, expiring. There is deliberately no RLS policy exposing this table to anon — token lookup happens in a server route under the service role, the staff_invites pattern.
Set by the atomic claim inside submit_form_response. A route-side check followed by an insert would be a race; this column moves in the same transaction as the response it authorises.

g.title: public.organizations
g.text: Tenant root. Single row today; every domain table hangs off organization_id for future multi-tenancy.

g.title: public.form_versions
g.text: One immutable published shape of a form. APPEND-ONLY BY DESIGN: no update or delete policy exists, so Postgres denies both, and the revoke below states that intent out loud. Editing a form means inserting a new version. That immutability is what lets a response REFERENCE the shape it answered instead of copying it — change a version in place and every response that points at it silently changes meaning.

Ordered array of field descriptors: [{"key","label","type","required","sensitive"}]. sensitive=true routes an answer to form_response_health instead of form_responses.answers — it is the switch that decides whether an answer needs clients.notes.health.view to read. Postgres cannot validate this shape; the server route that accepts submissions is the only enforcement, which is why it is the tested one.
The waiver/consent copy shown with THIS version. Copied onto each response at submit (form_responses.consent_text) — the reference here is provenance; the copy there is the legal record.

g.title: public.form_links:form_version_id->public.form_versions:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (form_version_id) REFERENCES form_versions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

g.title: public.clients
g.text: Spa clients (no auth accounts). no_show_count is maintained by trigger from appointment status changes. flags is an extensible jsonb for operational booleans (requires_card_on_file).
Operational booleans, extendable without migrations. Known keys: requires_card_on_file
Stripe Customer id (cus_...). Created lazily by the setup-intent route on first card save. Single platform Stripe account; a future Connect retrofit would add an account dimension here.

g.title: public.form_links:client_id->public.clients:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (client_id) REFERENCES clients(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

g.title: public.staff
g.text: Employees. Linked 1:1 to auth.users via user_id. Deactivated (active=false), never deleted. Self-editable personal fields are guarded by trg_guard_staff_self_update.
Whether this person appears as a provider in scheduling (columns, qualification pickers, slot search).

g.title: public.form_responses
g.text: One filled-in form. answers holds ONLY the non-sensitive answers; anything the version marks sensitive is in form_response_health, behind clients.notes.health.view. No authenticated INSERT policy exists on purpose: a submission must be validated against its version's field list, Postgres cannot check jsonb shape, so writes go through a server route under the service role and the validator is the enforcement.

The subject, when an existing client fills a waiver. Nullable because phase 2 adds prospect_intake_id for people who have no client record yet, and widens form_responses_subject to "exactly one subject". Until then the check requires a client.

Physical snapshot of the consent copy this person actually agreed to, readable without joining the version. Same discipline as the card-consent policy_text snapshot: the legal record must not depend on a lookup years later.
The subject when the person had no client record. Cascades: purging a prospect takes their answers with them, which is what the 30-day retention promise means.
Which issued link produced this response. Audit trail, not authorization — the link is consumed by then. Nulls on delete so a tidied link cannot orphan a response.

g.title: public.form_responses:form_link_id->public.form_links:id
g.text: FOREIGN KEY (form_link_id) REFERENCES form_links(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
